notes: Background: Arkadia builds a blended search + answers layer for large enterprise customers (legal, pharma). Heavy emphasis on precision at top-k and auditability.
Current infra: hybrid vector index (on-cloud), bi-encoder embeddings based on older SBERT fork; ranking currently done client-side with a lightweight pairwise model.
Pain: quality regressions when trying newer embeddings; slow migration path for reranker — wants eval-driven plan with A/B and canary to avoid surfacing regressions in production.
Scale: indexing plan ~100M documents, ~10k QPS peak for search layer (burst), typical steady QPS ~800. Index size projected 6-8 TB vectors (float16/quantized options under consideration).
Latency targets: p99 < 250ms for search+rerank combined (EU region), p50 < 60ms. Cost goal: <$0.02 per complex query (embeddings + rerank) for steady-state.
Model preferences: prefer open-models with reproducible evals; interested in Redwood-recommended quantized variants and a staged cross-encoder reranker for top-10 reordering.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, audit logs for every query, and EU data residency for EU customers.
Commercial: leaning toward Dedicated if performance guarantees hold; hosted API acceptable for initial eval if we can validate cost/latency at scale.
Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'We will not accept any net-negative NDCG on core legal queries — rollouts must be eval-proven with canary and automatic rollback.'
SE notes: propose 2-phase eval: (1) offline evals (held-out legal query sets, fairness/regression checks), (2) shadow canary on 5% traffic with telemetry and auto-fallback to current reranker.
Requested artifacts: detailed cost model for 3 index/quantization configs, sample eval report template, suggested canary policy (metrics + thresholds).
Redwood asks: provide ingestion checklist, kv/prefix cache recommendations for legal doc prefixes, and example A/B test dashboard for eval metrics.
Sales play: free 30-day pilot credits, dedicated SE hours for integration, SOW for dedicated capacity quoted in drive deck.
Other references: internal eval harness repo link stub, shared prompt/eval deck in Drive.
Tone: pragmatic, engineering-first; decision driven by eval artifacts not anecdotes.
